images.works: The nine states are distinct and in the right order. Columns go dark to light (indigo-slate, teal, green-gold with bed dapples and a glow above), matching WaterColours (PoolsScene.cs:1218-1227). Rows go hot to cold (steam, plain, frost). Light changes only the water and Heat only the rim and air, so the two channels stay separate as the requirements ask. The ice-blue frost crust still reads on a cream lip even in the bright column (bottom-right panel), and steam reads well over the slate backdrop. Use it as the legend for the pool card's plane.
images.problems: 1) The backdrop is flat slate-grey, not the requested cream travertine, so the pale-stone worst case for steam was never tested. Its tone also drifts by column (darker on the left, yellow haze on the right). 2) Steam does fade where it crosses the beam (top-right panel, upper right), which confirms the requirement. But the beam appears only in the hot row, which ties 'sun' to Heat. In game the beam stays fixed on the top bowl, and a hot Shade Pool gets no beam, so ignore the beam as a Heat cue. 3) The lantern looks lit in column 3, rows 2-3 (its pane glows), so the control fails there. 4) The warm and cool shallows barely show (only an orange smear near one fish in the hot row, no cool tint in the cold row), so Heat reads only through steam and frost. That matches the code's subtle shallows lerp, so Heat from -1 to +1 is invisible. 5) Fish and snails are drawn floating on the surface with ripple rings and are untinted by the water. In code, snails sit at FloorY+0.01 and the water is drawn over all creatures at alpha 0.5-0.92 (draw order PoolsScene.cs:1019-1030), so dark water will hide them far more than shown. 6) The code is much weaker than this image: steam is small puffs at alpha 0.22 (:830-840), and frost is just 5 glints of 0.12 m (:1280-1285), not a rim crust.

images.works: The clarity row reads in order (silted, half-cleared, clear). The thriving panel (three warm, high fish) and the egg-carrier (plump beside a slim mate) read well. The Lantern Reed panel is the best one: the candle-like tip glows, and warm-gold sun-motes are easy to tell from pale-blue frost-motes against the dark mossy wall. That shows motes need a dark backdrop.
images.problems: 1) The silted panel (top-left) is pale chartreuse under the beam, too close to the Light+ water in the energy grid, so silt could be misread as Light. The shader mixes murk toward olive-grey (0.42, 0.45, 0.33) (Shaders.cs:258); keep that, not this colour. 2) The clear panel (top-right) loses both fish, so it is no longer the same pool. The half-cleared panel has a hard vertical split down the middle, but code murk is uniform. 3) The mood row swaps species (whiskered carp or catfish in place of Spotted Spinners) and changes the water colour per panel. In code a sulking fish keeps its species tint, darkened 35% toward StoneDark, and stays low (PoolsScene.cs:1094, 850-856). Mood must never look like a different fish. 4) Hush-Moss (bottom-left) lies across the front half of the bed. Code roots plants along the back, and the front is where laid objects and soak rings sit. 5) The snails (bottom-centre) are huge and swim on the surface with wakes. They are off the rims but not on the bed. 6) The vessel is a round tub on a pedestal, not the 2.4:1 travertine oval. 7) Some motes drift far up the wall (bottom-right). In code motes hover 0.3-0.65 m above the water.

images.works: This is the best room-scale state frame. Live state wins over the set: the root-shaded bottom pool reads as bright, yet the blue-grey boulders, roots and runnel fall still identify it. The top pool stays the beam pool. Frost on the middle pool's cream lip reads instantly as ice. Steam shows against the dark wet wall left of the beam. Fish (about 50 px) and snails (about 30 px) are near code scale at 1600x900. HUD check passes at 1600x900: nothing essential sits under the clock, title band, tabs, corner buttons or satchel bar. The filled spare bowl reads as a fourth pool with its own lantern.
images.problems: Coordinates are at 1600x900. 1) The Spawning Pond holds a yellow fish, a grey fish and a snail (about 683-900, 484-528). That breaks its identity and teaches the wrong rule. 2) The frost is a raised crust with icicles over the front lip and down the terrace face (about 509-838, 515-608). It hides the front of the bed where laid objects and soaks sit, and the code cannot draw it. 3) The Sun-Lens and its soak ring sit mid-pool on the top bowl (about 1034-1112, 310-348), not at the front of the bed, so the 'most grazing bed' test is unanswered. 4) Steam veils the right half of the cave mouth and the brook (about 990-1068, 124-273). 5) The brightened Shade Pool shows three glowing Grey Guppies. In lifeforms.json Grey Guppies thrive only at Light ≤2 and survive to 3, so at this brightness the game shows them dim and low. 6) The egg-carrier is drawn as a round pink pufferfish; code only scales the fish 1.28x. 7) Snails float on the surface again. 8) The pale-blue motes over the middle pool read as runnel spray against the pale riser. 9) The green-capped fern pot (850-940, 560-665) looks like a second stool beside the real one (980-1060, 595-680), so the click target is ambiguous.

images.works: The Spawning Pond keeps its identity: only the reed, small Shade-Salt crystals near its front, and a few blue motes, with no fish or snails. The bright Shade Pool still reads as the Shade Pool. Steam is visible only where it crosses the dark wall left of the beam and is lost inside the beam (about 1050-1220, 140-300 at 1600). That confirms the requirement to set steam against dark rock. The HUD check passes as in variant a.
images.problems: Coordinates are at 1600x900. 1) Frost is drawn as breaking surf on the middle rim (about 495-1095, 425-600). It reads as splashing water and contradicts 'perfectly still' (pools.json:41). Variant a's frost is the one to follow. 2) The top pool has lost its Spotted Spinners and shows only snails. At Light 5 / Heat 2 the Spinners thrive (thrive light 0..5, heat 1..4) and should be glowing. 3) The Sun-Lens is a handled magnifying glass inside a large ring at the pool centre (about 1010-1180, 300-355). It is confusable with the Magnifying Glass tool (AGENTS.md open question 14). The game draws an 'assembled' item as a pebble (PoolsScene.cs:1071-1074), so neither image shows what the game shows. 4) An egg cluster is drawn under a fish (about 530, 745). Code has no eggs or fry. 5) Hush-Moss covers the Shade Pool's laid-object spot (379, 784).

images.works: The night frame stays cozy and readable. The walls are deep blue and never black. Warm light is carried down by the three pool lanterns and the ledger candle. The pools keep their identities by colour and silhouette: olive top, clear teal middle, dark bottom. The cave mouth is a dim blue doorway with the small lamp of the hub steps, which matches the hub. The reed tip, the faintly glowing snails (they emit Light +1) and the warm motes read beautifully on the dark riser. The left third is quiet. At 1600x900, every HUD area falls on dark wall.
images.problems: 1) The middle pool is the brightest thing in the room, as if lit from within. Its live Light is 1 (base 0, reed +1), below the glow-above threshold of 2, so in engine only its lantern lights it. 2) The crock's dim lamp is missing; code has one (PoolsScene.cs:193). 3) Motes over the Spawning Pond would not exist at the start state, because nothing is laid yet. 4) The top pool is drawn clear, with crisp fish and snails, not the 85% silt of the start state. 5) The Shade water is violet (about 230-640, 650-790 at 1600). Code is slate-indigo and the prose says green. 6) Hush-Moss again lies across the front of the Shade Pool's bed. Lamp budget: pool lanterns, ledger, crock and the mouth lamp come to 6, or 7 with the spare bowl's lantern, inside the cap of 8 (PoolsScene.cs:992). A further pool's lantern would light no lamp.

images.works: It works as key art and as an answer to the oculus question. It shows a round opening of pale sky fringed with ferns, one thick hanging root, a sliver of cut stone at the rim, and a slanting beam with motes. Hub continuity is right: steps on the left of the mouth, brook falling on its right into the top pool, roots sweeping down the left wall into a root stair. The bottom pool keeps its identity: dark mossy blue-grey lip, indigo-slate water, two small grey fish.
images.problems: 1) The pools are full-width shelves that cascade over dams through the middle pool. There is no bypass runnel, no reed, and no sign of the Spawning Pond's stillness. It shows the cascade route, not the chosen one. 2) The brook leaves a separate cleft beside the mouth, not the mouth's right half. 3) The masonry arc on the oculus rim (top-right) reads as a built well-head, which suggests an opening the hub would have to show. That conflicts with the scarp-shelf proposal (section.png). 4) Its many thin roots at the left would become ink noise in the engine. As its purpose says, derive no layout or kit from it.

images.works: The courtyard side is right in parts: the water gate's arch with its portcullis rusted up near the crown, the narrow gallery bridging it, and a low mossy outcrop with a door-high mouth that the courtyard stream runs into. The finish is pleasant.
images.problems: It inverts the descent that section.png sets. 1) The pools sit far above courtyard level: the top pool's water is at about y 520 against the cobbles at y 1000-1300 (original px), roughly 6 m up. In section.png the Sunward water is at world -6.0, 6 m below the courtyard. 2) The passage is a U. It dips from the outcrop to a low point, then a stair climbs up into the cave (about x 1130-1330, y 900-1300). The brook runs down that stair out of the room into a sump that also takes the courtyard stream, so it never falls into the top pool. 3) The wall is drawn as a face, not cut, so its 3.6 m thickness and the stair passing under its footings are missing. 4) There is no scarp-shelf ground at -1 beyond the wall; the oculus opens into solid grey. 5) It shows four or five pools with extra small basins, the outcrop sits beside the arch rather than inside it, and the arch is about half its 7.2 m width. Keep section.png as the guide. If the designer wants an illustrated cutaway, render it free from Blender rather than regenerating: add the wall slab, tunnel and scarp shelf to the blockout_flat.py scene, render side-on and orthographic, then paint over the result.

cross_cutting: Heat cues in code are far weaker than in any image. Steam is small puffs at alpha 0.22 (PoolsScene.cs:830-840). Frost is 5 glints of 0.12 m (:1280-1285). The shallows tint is at most a 0.35/0.45 lerp. The energy grid shows Heat reads only with a rim-wide ice-blue frost tint and a visible steam plume. Build: tint the rim toward #CFE8F6, scaled by -Heat (bowls need per-bowl rim parts for hover anyway), and add more glints. Keep frost flat, with no crust or icicles over the near lip. Make steam larger and denser, and let it rise against the dark wet wall left of the beam, not into the beam. Make the frost tint unlit, or strong enough to survive each pool lantern's warm light (radius 5.2).

Every image draws fish and snails floating on the surface, untinted by the water. In game, snails sit on the bed (FloorY+0.01), and the water is drawn over all creatures at alpha 0.5-0.92. Expect much fainter creatures in dark or murky water, so do not treat these frames as proof that creatures read. Creature scale at 1600x900 is close to code: fish about 45-50 px, snails about 25-30 px.

The front strip of every bed must stay clear. Hush-Moss is painted across the front of the Shade Pool in residents, both tended frames and night, covering its laid-object spot (379, 784 at 1600). Soak rings are painted mid-pool. Code roots plants along the back and lays objects at the front, so keep that. The 'soak ring on the most grazing bed' test is still unanswered: at the top pool the code's ring is only about 41x10 px. Check it in the Blender camera or in game.

Motes need a darker backdrop. The riser behind the Spawning Pond (the top terrace's front face, about x 560-1000, y 380-450 at 1600) is pale apricot, and by day pale-blue frost-motes and gold sun-motes vanish against it, as tended a and b show. The night frame shows how well they read on dark. Darken that riser with a wet moss band or a shadowed overhang. Also confine the 26 room dust motes (PoolsScene.cs:159, LanternHot glows over the whole room) to the beam, or they will read as sun-motes over the Spawning Pond.

Pool identity has to come from architecture and residents, not water colour. The beam and apricot flowstone mark the top pool, the reed and smooth lip mark the middle, and the boulders, roots and runnel fall mark the bottom. This holds in every room frame even when the Shade Pool is brightened. Keep fish and snails out of the Spawning Pond in any reference (tended-a breaks this).

The three green-capped fern pots (blockout decor, about 645-710,205-275; 850-940,560-665; 1435-1510,260-340 at 1600) read as extra stools. The middle one stands next to the real stool hotspot. The kit should make them unmistakable pots with fronds.

HUD check at 1600x900: all four room frames pass. When shown, the hover caption covers the Shade Pool's right third (x 480-700, y 663-764), and toasts can cover the top pool's back-right rim and lantern (x 1160-1366, y 280-300). Both are transient. The spare bowl is cut by the right and bottom edges (x 1290-1600, y 510-900), and the ±53 px sway can push it further, so it relies on focus and tabs.

Content and code contradictions. (a) Shade water: the finishes and night frame paint it violet, the code's dark end is slate-indigo (#4C6A88/#1E2A48), and pools.json:24 says 'green and tired'. Do not copy the violet; the designer's call stands. (b) pools.json:41 says the Spawning Pond is 'ringed with flat stones', but the images give the boulder ring to the Shade Pool and the Spawning Pond a smooth cream lip. Either give it a low flat-stone ring that keeps the front of the bed visible, or rewrite the line. (c) Grey Guppies thrive only at Light ≤2 (lifeforms.json), so a Shade Pool brightened beyond that shows sulking guppies, not glowing ones. (d) At start, Sunward's live Light is 3 (base 1 plus the two snails' +1 each), but the glow above it is scaled by (1 - murk) = 0.15 (PoolsScene.cs:1278-1279), so the finish's 'soft glow above the silted top pool' will not appear until the pool is cleansed. (e) The Sun-Lens (kind 'assembled') is drawn as a pebble; whether it gets a lens-like prop is a designer call, and it should not be a handled magnifier (open question 14).

images.works: Every requested piece is there, and they read as 3D forms with clean ink and flat banded colour, so they are buildable in the toon shader with the inverted-hull outline. Dry bowl (top left): thick rolled lip, a pale mineral ring and leaf litter on the bed. That is lathe/sweep plus leaf() decals. Terrace block (top centre): the bowl sits at the block's front corner, so its front lip is the top of the flowstone face. That is the right construction for the top pool's dam (layout top_edge puts the face 0.08-0.2 m in front of the oval). Its banded cream and tan strata can come from painted() with a horizontal-band term. Shaft-wall slab (top right): broad vertical drapes, which surface() can make with a displacement that varies along x and stays nearly constant along y. Cave mouth (bottom left): door-sized round-headed ring with a stone sill. Steps are on the LEFT and the brook channel on the RIGHT, the handedness the hub requires. Low outflow arch: an arch-ring tube plus a recess in the wall surface, the same trick pools_grotto.py already uses for the river tunnel. Roots (right): only 3 thick tapered roots, each with one fork, no thin strands. Each is a root_tube bezier plus one smaller branch tube. Root stair: treads cut into a log, flanked by flaring side roots, which is cuboid treads plus root_tube flanks. Moss mounds and fern clumps map straight onto mound() and frond().
images.problems: 1) Not to scale. Against the 5.9 m bowl, the mouth comes out about 3.4 m wide (the room needs 1.4 x 1.6 m), and the stair, moss and ferns are oversized too. Take the forms only and take sizes from layout.py and PoolsScene. 2) Terrace-block lip (top centre) is a ring of ~40 scalloped beads with drip tips on the face. At 11-16 m every bead gets its own outline, which is ink noise, and the chosen finish frame has smooth rolled lips. Build a smooth lip with low jitter and paint the nodules into the texture. Keep face ribs 0.25 m or wider, with blunt ends. 3) Dry bowl is a freestanding deep tub: depth is about 1/4 of its length, against the 0.68 m needed on 5.9 m (lip +0.78, bed +0.1 from slot base). Use its lip and bed dressing only, as a sunk bowl. 4) 'Dam run with spill notch' (top centre-right) came out as a water-filled gutter with no drop. Reuse it as the runnel's flat U-channel with the painted water removed (the game draws water). The runnel still needs chute pieces down the 1.5 m faces. 5) Shaft slab is cream. The finish frame's walls are grey-blue, and steam needs a dark wall behind it, so keep the drape geometry and use the frame's colour. 6) Mouth steps sit OUTSIDE the arch, descending toward the viewer. In the layout the sill (y 2.4) is level with the landing, and the stair rises INSIDE the tunnel toward the hub. The tunnel interior is plain dark with no inner steps and no emissive daylight end. 7) 'Landing' is a thin irregular paver. The room needs a 0.74 m banded block (sill 2.4 down to the top terrace at 1.66) for the bag. 8) Roots have flat sawn ends, so bury the thick end in the wall or run it out of frame. Bark is plain brown; keep stoic-bark.png as in pools_grotto.py.

images.works: All 11 props are present and readable. Druids' bag (top centre): a drawstring bucket bag with a leather base band, oak-leaf embroidery and a shoulder strap. It reads as the druids' bag, not a satchel, which settles the brief/frame satchel problem. Ledger (top right): a reading slope that rises away from the viewer, so the page faces +Z. Its candle sits on an iron side bracket at +x, which matches the contract's candle at x 0.38-0.45. A green ink pot and reed pen add character. Stool on a round coiled reed mat: a lathe seat plus 3 beams, and a lathe disc with a ring texture for the mat. Two rakes: a wooden head bar with dowel tines and a ferrule. The leaning one (tines down) is exactly the rake key's pose: head at origin, handle +Y. Crook-stake lantern with a square cage, the Stillkeeper's Sieve (wooden hoop, brass mesh), a plank shelf of 5 lidded jars on brackets, a fern pot, and a slotted drain grate. All are cuboid, lathe, tube and frond work. Crock: two-tone glaze dip line, rolled rim bead, cleated wooden lid and long-handled net.
images.problems: 1) Crock (top left) is a tall jar, about as tall as it is wide or taller. The contract is squat: rim top 0.70 m, opening r 0.52, belly r 0.675 (pools_room.py CROCK). Keep the CROCK profile and take only the glaze split (put the material break near 0.45 m in mat(i)) and the cleated lid. Side bug in the current kit: the lid is r 0.45, smaller than the r 0.52 opening; make it about r 0.62. 2) Ledger slope sits on the floor with no stand, so the book would be at about 0.35 m. Mount the sheet's slope box on the existing trestle (top at 1.08 m, tilt 0.42). Move the candle bracket to the side midpoint (z about 0.05, candle top 1.12-1.2), and put the ink pot on a small side shelf near 0.95 m, not the floor. 3) Bag: build the body about 1.0 m tall with the gathered frill reaching about 1.1 m. Leave a small dark opening in the gather so the game's glow at 1.18 m reads as coming from inside. Keep the strap inside the 1.1 x 0.9 m hotspot footprint, and make the drawstring and embroidery texture, not tubes. 4) Inconsistent scale across the sheet: the fern pot is about crock height, and the stool's seat is about half its height wide. Use code sizes: POT 0.45 m tall, r 0.39; stool seat top 0.55, seat r 0.25-0.30, mat r about 0.55. 5) Net mesh and sieve mesh are fine line hatching, which turns into ink noise. Keep them as textured surfaces, as the existing M.net lathe does. 6) Lantern crook is drawn brown like wood; the brief said iron. The 3-4 cm staff will read as a single ink line at 13 m, which is acceptable. 7) The top half of the sheet carries a cave background and the noon beam, which washes out the ledger pages. It is still readable, so there is no need to regenerate.

images.works: This is the finish the kit should match, and most of its forms are buildable. Smooth flat-topped rolled lips of even width, about 0.25-0.3 m (top, middle, bottom pools). The top pool's lip runs straight into its flowstone dam face (centre right). Banded cream and peach terrace faces with moss draping over their top edges (centre left). Grey-blue shaft walls with soft vertical streaks behind the cream terraces give the value contrast the requirements ask for. A blue-grey mossy boulder ring round the Shade pool (bottom left) gives it a darker rim where frost will read. The bypass runnel is a sunk channel along the top terrace, a chute down the left face, then a fall into the bottom pool, which also keeps the middle pool still. The mouth (top centre) shows steps rising inside the tunnel, a bright daylight end, and the brook spilling from its right half. The bag sits on a banded landing block left of the mouth.
images.problems: Several shapes are blockout leftovers to replace with kit pieces, not copy: green cylinders at the FERNS positions (top terrace left, mid terrace) should be fern pots; the grey box with a book on top (centre right) should be the ledger stand; the flap-and-buckle satchel on the landing should be the druids' bucket bag from the props sheet; the grey stone cylinder with a rake handle in it should be the squat crock; the short square post lanterns should be the crook lanterns at the code position; the straight pole 'roots' crossing at left should be tapered forked roots; and the plank stair at left should be the root stair. The spare bowl (bottom right, cropped) stands as a raised freestanding tub. Per layout.py it is a sunk bowl at slot y 0 with its rim at the mid terrace (0.16), so build it sunk. Near boulders round the bottom pool look 0.6-0.8 m tall. Keep their tops 0.4 m or less above the floor (-1.34) so the front of the bed, where laid objects and soak rings sit, stays visible at 35 deg. Taller boulders belong at the sides and back. The runnel water is drawn at terrace-top level; see cross-cutting note 2. Baked steam, glow and crystal-clear water are live state, so nothing about them goes in the kit.

images.works: Use it for forms only. Its rimstone lips are thick and rounded and curl slightly outward over the dam faces. That is the profile to sweep round each oval: inner wall, rounded crown, small outward overhang, then the face. Dam faces have vertical nodular flowstone columns (centre), which can be broad displacement ribs. The single spill notches cut down into the lip show how the top pool's overflow notch into the runnel should look. The dry round basin at the right, set into the terrace, shows a sunk spare bowl. The slab stair against the left wall shows the second root-stair flight.
images.problems: Layout is not usable. The mouth is upper left, under the HUD clock, title and tabs. Water cascades through the middle pool, which contradicts the bypass. A mass of thin hanging roots (left) would be pure ink noise. The micro-terraced floor (bottom right) has dozens of tiny lips; at most 2-3 broad steps are buildable. The photographic travertine texture, water glitter and depth cues cannot be drawn by the two-band toon shader. Paint the nodular character into the texture and keep the geometry smooth.

images.works: This is the layout the kit must reproduce at the game camera: three terrace levels, the mouth and landing at the back centre-right, the runnel bypass on the left, the ledge furniture right of the middle pool, the spare bowl at the right edge and the beam from the top right. It agrees with layout.py, which is where the kit's coordinates should come from.
images.problems: Its props are blockout primitives: cylinders for fern pots, a box for the ledger, a satchel. The spare bowl is again drawn as a raised tub. Treat it as a placement reference only, with no forms taken from it.

cross_cutting: Kit contract gap: the game builds bowls, lanterns, trickle, spill and river itself (BuildBasin, PoolsScene.cs:323-360), and Prop() only asks for shell, decor, ferns, crock, bag, ledger, stool and rake. Any bowl, lantern, sieve, runnel water or beam from the kit needs a matching code change. Recommended contract: one 'bowl' part (plus optional per-slot overrides such as a wet blue-grey variant for the Shade pool), built in the POOL'S LOCAL FRAME. Origin at the slot base (water minus 0.62), long axis +X, front +Z, inner lip at the largest oval (rx 2.96, rz 1.22), lip top +0.78, bed +0.1, with the crook lantern baked in so its cage holds the code's 0.16 x 0.22 x 0.16 glow box at (0.82rx, 1.32, -0.62rz). The code then draws it with tk.World exactly as it draws tk.Stone today, so the hover rim and lift keep working. A smaller-capacity pool can scale it by (rx/2.96, 1, rz/1.22).

Runnel elevation bug in layout.py: RUNNEL starts at y 1.64-1.68 beside a top pool whose water is at 1.5, so it flows uphill, and on the mid terrace it sits at 0.19 above a 0.16 terrace. The kit must cut a U-channel 0.25 m or more into each terrace. The overflow notch cuts the top lip down to the water at 1.5, the channel water falls from 1.48 or lower, and on the mid level the water stays near 0.0 inside 0.16 walls. Model the channel dry and let the game draw the water along kit markers.

Ellipse helper trap: lathe(scale=(rx, ry)) scales radial offsets, so a lip swept that way is 2.4x wider at the ends (about 0.3 m) than at the sides (about 0.12 m). Lips and the runnel need a small sweep(profile, path, closed) helper that offsets along the curve normal (tube() generalised to an open or closed profile). Curved dam faces need arc-length UVs, because BoxUV switches axis at 45 deg and breaks the painted banding.

Markers are positions only (ModelAsset.Markers is a Vector3 map), so pool-N markers that replace Slots cannot carry yaw. Add a second marker per pool (for example 'pool-3-axis' at the long-axis end), or encode yaw in the name. Parts are matched to meshes by material and vertex count (ModelAsset.MatchParts), so geometrically identical parts in one glb can be swapped. Either reuse one local-frame bowl part, or give per-slot parts distinct vertex counts.

Neither sheet shows these pieces the room needs: (a) the runnel U-channel sunk in the terraces, with the overflow notch and two chutes, down the 1.5 m top dam face and the 1.66 m drop into the bottom pool; (b) terrace faces at 1.5 m (top dam following the top pool's curved front, mid dam to the bottom floor, the right-hand top-terrace face along z -3.35 out to x 8.4, the ledge front at z 3.3) and at 0.74 m (the landing block for the bag); (c) a smooth sunk bowl lip in cream and in wet blue-grey; (d) the Shade pool's boulder ring, low at the front; (e) spare-bowl alcoves for pools 4 and up cut into the right wall beyond x 8.4, each holding a full 5.9 x 2.4 m sunk dry bowl and its markers, with wall continuing far enough right for the focus camera; (f) the mouth tunnel interior with steps rising toward the hub and an emissive daylight end, plus the brook spout lip in the sill's right half; (g) the right-hand wall return out to x 8 or more for focus close-ups; (h) the wet blue-grey bottom floor and the outflow channel under the low arch; (i) moss drapes painted onto face tops (texture, not geometry); (j) the noon beam as an additive mesh, which is a code part; (k) new spots for the drain grate and feed shelf, because DRAIN (-0.9, 1.0) and LEDGE no longer exist in this layout.

Size source of truth: neither sheet is to scale. Take every dimension from layout.py (pool centres and levels: top water 1.5, mid 0, bottom -1.5, spare 0 at yaw pi/2; terraces 1.66, 0.16, -1.34; sill 2.4; stair flights of 4 x 0.185 m and 6 x 0.25 m rises) and from the pools_room.py prop contract. Have the kit script read those values directly, not copy code constants (the warning about CRACK_X in pools_grotto.py).

Designer decision: the bowl bed below the waterline should be mid-dark, not cream. The water shader's alpha runs 0.5-0.92 over the bed, so a cream bed would make every pool look milky. That leaves cream only on the lip and a narrow mineral ring just under the surface. The finish frame hides this, because its water is opaque.

Ordered kit build list: 1) Read layout.py values; add markers pool-0..3 (+axis), brook start, runnel path points, mouth light and beam spot. 2) Helpers: sweep() for constant-width lips and the U-channel, a banded painted() variant, arc-length UVs. 3) Shell massing: the three terrace levels plus the landing block from top_level_poly, mid_level_poly and the floor, with flowstone dam faces (1.5, 1.5 and 0.74 m) and painted moss. 4) The local-frame 'bowl' part with lantern (cream, plus a blue-grey Shade variant), with mineral ring and leaf litter for the dry spare. 5) Runnel channel, overflow notch and two chutes, modelled dry. 6) Mouth: arch ring, split sill, tunnel stair, daylight plane, brook spout. 7) Grey-blue drape shaft walls round the back, left and right to x 8.4 and beyond, up out of frame, with the right-wall alcoves. 8) Bottom level: wet floor, low-front boulder ring, outflow arch and channel. 9) Four thick forked roots in stoic bark, and the two-flight root stair. 10) Props: crock (existing profile, glaze split, r 0.62 lid), bag (drawstring bucket, about 1.1 m mouth), ledger (sheet's slope on the existing trestle, side candle), stool on a round mat, wooden-head rake plus a leaning decor rake, sieve, feed shelf, fern pots, grate. 11) Decor and ferns: moss mounds and frond() clumps. Then the code changes: Prop keys for bowl, lantern, sieve and beam, markers in place of Slots, runnel water threaded along the markers, BagPos y 2.4, and the focus clamp.
